1408.title: Bug: carried MSM resource-cleanup patches write through an uninitialized pointer
1408.body:
Found during T41 (#688), accepted Stage-B finding F-01 / L-01 and Stage-C punch item PL-001. **Severity: High. Owner: the base integration (#563/#559).** This is a source defect in the audited fork, not a report of an observed crash. The T41 lane makes no source fix.

## Source trace

At audited source `02aab33bd9842610b0d466c9c186454dc14373ee` (unchanged from dispatch `d7dd766659`), both files contain the pre-fix version:

- `projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux/patches/7.0/0010-msm-resource-cleanup.patch`
- `projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux/patches/7.2/0010-msm-resource-cleanup.patch`

The first diff adds `cstate->num_mixers = 0;` at patch line 19; `cstate = to_dpu_crtc_state(crtc_state);` remains later, at patch line 37. In the **complete final SM8550 patched function**, the local pointer is declared at line 1441, written through at 1453 and first assigned at 1470. The full function has no earlier initialization; the global-state error return does not initialize the successful path. SM8550's configuration enables `CONFIG_DRM_MSM=y` at line 4461. H700 and GENERIC_X64 do not enable that driver in the configurations read. Both carried patch copies are byte-identical.

Expected: initialize the local pointer before its first dereference. Actual: the first field write precedes initialization. This permits an indeterminate-pointer write on an enabled MSM DPU path. The accepted normal applications all succeed; application success does not establish code correctness.

[Complete final function and numbered trace](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/7e5d1546712df2eb79c585fce663186770d1ceb9/docs/audits/2026_11_02-epic-m6-patches-shipped-kernel/stage-b/corrected/0010-final-function.txt), [accepted refutation](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/7e5d1546712df2eb79c585fce663186770d1ceb9/docs/audits/2026_11_02-epic-m6-patches-shipped-kernel/04-analysis.md#finding-verification-phase-45).

## Existing upstream fix

[9416eec2c200ad969d9e421e686fc7cbfdaca36a](https://github.com/ROCKNIX/distribution/commit/9416eec2c200ad969d9e421e686fc7cbfdaca36a), `kernel: msm dp resource cleanup patch fix uninit pointer`, states:

> Previous version writes to field pointed by an uninitialized pointer.

The immutable local history shows the fix moves initialization before the write in both copies. The retained two-path comparison of the audited source against pinned upstream `651150fc88` reports:

```text
2 files changed, 28 insertions(+), 22 deletions(-)
```

Route uptake through the existing base integration; do not repair these carried patches on the T41 audit branch. No upstream submission is needed for an already-fixed upstream defect.

**Already written:** H700, SM8550 and GENERIC_X64 image builds using the fork's pre-fix source since the base consume these pre-fix patch bytes; this audit did not inspect built images or installed devices. Only SM8550's enabled affected driver is established by the configurations read. The base merge corrects future source/builds; installed images remain unchanged until their normal update. No storage schema, migration or cloud write is introduced by this source correction, and no existing device state was read or changed by this audit.

**Can this be done on the VM?** No — the tree, history and accepted final touched-source artifact establish this source defect; nothing a guest shows is a provenance fact. Build, guest and physical-runtime qualification remain outside this source-only lane. No runtime occurrence or runtime fix is claimed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The base integration records `fixed-at` and the contemporaneous `upstream/next` commit; after the merge, `git diff --stat <fixed-at> upstream/next -- projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux/patches/7.0/0010-msm-resource-cleanup.patch projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux/patches/7.2/0010-msm-resource-cleanup.patch` is empty, with the two hashes and command output retained.
- [ ] A source trace for both corrected siblings places `cstate = to_dpu_crtc_state(crtc_state)` before the first `cstate->num_mixers` write and cites the integration commit carrying upstream `9416eec2c200ad969d9e421e686fc7cbfdaca36a`; the issue retains this Already written/VM account and `tools/box-check --issue <this issue>` reports 0 fail.

Filed by Codex / GPT-6-Astra / xhigh, T3 `m6-t3-emulators`, session `01a19d12-29e3-7fe0-9f41-038dac0a5deb`; identity observed in the live Herdr footer, not provider-attested. Reactive bug: no milestone or parent.

1410.title: ppsspp-sa: home-pause patch creates a nested patch instead of changing SDL
1410.body:
T42 source audit F-T42-01 / PL-01 found that the selected PPSSPP patch creates an inert nested patch instead of changing the intended SDL source. This is a reactive bug, with no milestone or parent; #689 owns the audit record, and the standalone-emulator owner (#677 context) owns any future correction.

## Source trace

Reviewed source: `9dd0716033f8831ffbd0b5ee8efbb5e5a066cfb1`.

- `projects/ROCKNIX/packages/emulators/standalone/ppsspp-sa/package.mk:5` pins `afbc66a318b86432642b532c575241f3716642ef` (v1.20.2).
- Its `patches/007-disable-home-pause.patch:11–16` is an outer diff creating `package/batocera/emulators/ppsspp/007-disable-home-pause.patch`.
- Lines 17–29 are added text containing the intended `SDL/SDLJoystick.cpp` hunk, including GUIDE mapping `NKCODE_BACK` → `NKCODE_UNKNOWN`.
- `scripts/unpack:191–196` applies the outer patch once. The recipe's post_unpack hook only adjusts compiler flag files; no hook applies the created nested file.

Consequently this patch does not perform its advertised SDL change. A successful patch exit can conceal the defect. Fixed upstream `651150fc88` has a direct SDL diff returning `NKCODE_GUIDE`, a different mapping from the nested payload; importing it requires an explicit intended-behavior decision by the owning fix stream.

## Evidence and limits

`docs/audits/2026_11_02-epic-m6-patches-shipped/stage-b/nested-patch/receipt.json` retains a constructed fixture: GNU patch 2.8 diagnostic and normal rc 0, nested target created, sentinel SDLJoystick.cpp byte-identical. This proves the wrapper mechanism, not application at the actual PPSSPP pin or observed player behavior. Source/recipe/unpack readbacks and duplicate searches are under `stage-b/source-context/`. The sibling scan found one product-path instance; 23 other hits are legitimate historical product-diff evidence.

Severity: Medium. No data-loss or security consequence is demonstrated.

Already written: builds containing the outer patch may keep the preexisting SDL mapping and an inert nested file in their build source. This patch writes no player settings or cloud data. A correction must rebuild the affected binary and preserve existing `/storage`; editing the audit alone repairs no installed image.

Can this be done on the VM? The source-target regression can be proved from source fixtures without a guest. The later input-flow check can run in GENERIC_X64 with injected controller input; no physical fact is required. This issue grants no runtime allocation or device/cloud action.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A source regression fails on the reviewed wrapper, then passes on the chosen direct SDL diff: exact selected pin/stack, actual normal rc, before/after target hashes and absence of the nested patch file are retained.
- [ ] The intended GUIDE mapping is recorded and exercised in GENERIC_X64 with an agent-verifiable input trace/frame or equivalent deterministic event assertion, bound to the corrected installed binary identity.
- [ ] The fix's Already written record and upgrade/clean-install evidence show existing `/storage` settings are preserved; no cloud action is required by the correction.

## Proposed mechanism

Move the patch's written/routed intent to an audited source-target regression. A focused product-patch guard may reject inert nested patch targets, with explicit intentional exceptions; historical audit product-diff files are not product patches. The coordinator assigns a separate source-changing brief. T42 A–D makes no product edit and leaves this bug open.

Recorded by Codex / GPT-6-Astra / xhigh, OpenAI, T5 wN:p7, Local reader. No external reviewer.
